claims.text: Trace oxygen and nitrogen can be unintentionally introduced during alloy processing or thermal exposure.
Trace oxygen and nitrogen promote local solute depletion in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Trace oxygen and nitrogen destabilize the high-temperature BCC phase in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Interstitial impurities trigger secondary-phase formation during cooling and thermal aging.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 begins the proposed treatment in a high-temperature BCC state.
Interstitial enrichment creates local compositional inhomogeneities.
Impurity-enriched inhomogeneities act as nucleation sites for FCC, intermetallic, or other secondary phases.
Oxygen and nitrogen initially contribute to solid-solution strengthening.
During thermal exposure, oxygen and nitrogen diffuse and segregate.
Interstitial segregation depletes the surrounding matrix of solutes needed to stabilize the BCC phase.
The resulting local compositional change lowers the thermodynamic stability of BCC.
Lower BCC stability facilitates nucleation and growth of secondary phases.
Impurity-doped samples will form secondary phases earlier and in greater amounts than impurity-minimized samples.
Impurity-doped samples will exhibit mechanical-property changes relative to the impurity-minimized baseline.
Impurity-minimized Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 will remain predominantly BCC with little or no secondary-phase development.
The proposed mechanism applies when interstitial diffusion is thermally activated during moderate-temperature exposure.
The proposed mechanism requires impurity concentration to exceed a critical threshold.
The mechanism should not operate when interstitial impurities are eliminated or reduced below the critical threshold.
A Ti-V-Nb-Ta refractory high-entropy alloy aged at 700°C exhibited interstitial-associated phase segregation, depletion of solute interstitials from the matrix, and progressive softening.

Failure of impurity-doped samples to show a statistically significant increase in secondary-phase formation or associated mechanical-property changes relative to the impurity-minimized control would falsify the hypothesis.
